# Upgrading PHP

> Upgrade the host to PHP 8.5 for Pelican Panel and update NGINX, Apache or Caddy to use the new PHP-FPM version.

Source: https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/php-upgrade/

This documentation includes instructions for upgrading your system to the latest version of PHP. Please reference the
table below to check what PHP version you need for your version of Pelican.

| Panel Version | PHP Version        |
|---------------|--------------------|
| 1.x           | 8.5, 8.4           |

## Install PHP

In order to install PHP 8.5, you will need to run the following commands. Please keep in mind different operating systems
may have slightly different requirements for how these commands are formatted.

```bash
# Add additional repository for PHP
sudo add-apt-repository -y ppa:ondrej/php
sudo apt -y update

# Optional: Remove old PHP versions
sudo apt -y purge php*

# Install PHP 8.5
sudo apt -y install php8.5 php8.5-{gd,mysql,mbstring,bcmath,xml,curl,zip,intl,sqlite3,fpm}
```

## Webserver Configuration

### NGINX

After upgrading to PHP 8.5, you will most likely need to update your NGINX configuration. Your configuration file
is most likely called `pelican.conf` and located in the `/etc/nginx/sites-available/` directory, or if on CentOS,
`/etc/nginx/conf.d/`.

Make sure to update the path in the command below to reflect the actual location of your configuration file.

``` bash
sed -i -e 's/php[7|8].[0-9]-fpm.sock/php8.5-fpm.sock/' /etc/nginx/sites-available/pelican.conf
```

Once you have edited the file run the command below to reload NGINX and apply your changes.

```bash
systemctl reload nginx
```

### Apache

Run the commands below to disable all previous PHP versions and enable PHP 8.5 when serving requests.

``` bash
a2dismod php*
a2enmod php8.5
```

### Caddy

After upgrading to PHP 8.5, you will most likely need to update your Caddy configuration. Your configuration file
is most likely called `Caddyfile` and located in the `/etc/caddy/` directory.

Make sure to update the path in the command below to reflect the actual location of your configuration file.

``` bash
sed -i -e 's/php[7|8].[0-9]-fpm.sock/php8.5-fpm.sock/' /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
```

Once you have edited the file run the command below to restart Caddy and apply your changes.

```bash
systemctl restart caddy
```

---

# Database Hosts

> Add a MySQL or MariaDB database host to Pelican so servers can create their own databases, and fix common connection errors.

Source: https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/database-hosts/

Database hosts allow to create per-server databases on the given host.

## Database Configuration

### Create Database Host user

You will need a database user with the correct permissions before continuing any further.

Run the following commands to quickly create a user for your new database host:

```sql
mysql -u root -p

# Remember to change 'yourPassword' below to be a unique password
# Replace 127.0.0.1 with your panel ip if your panel and wings are on different machines
CREATE USER 'pelicanuser'@'127.0.0.1' IDENTIFIED BY 'yourPassword';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON *.* TO 'pelicanuser'@'127.0.0.1' WITH GRANT OPTION;
exit
```

### Allow external database access

Chances are you'll need to allow external access to this MySQL instance in order to allow servers to connect to it.

To do this, open `my.cnf`, which varies in location depending on your OS and how MySQL was installed. You can type `find /etc -iname my.cnf` to locate it.

Open `my.cnf`, add text below to the bottom of the file and save it:

```txt
[mysqld]
bind-address=0.0.0.0
```

Restart MySQL/ MariaDB to apply these changes. This will override the default MySQL configuration, which by default will only accept requests from localhost. Updating this will allow connections on all interfaces, and thus, external connections. Make sure to allow the MySQL port (default 3306) in your firewall.

## Panel Configuration

In the admin area of the panel, go to "Databases" and click the "New Database Host" button.

> **Tip**
>
> Users will later see the host as their database endpoint. Therefore, you should set it to a public ip or FQDN and not to `localhost` for example.

Hit "Create" and if everything was entered correctly you should be redirected to the database host list and see your new database host.

### Common issues

`Connection refused`:
Make sure that your database server is running and that you allowed external access to your database.

`Host '_______' is not allowed to connect to this MariaDB server`:
You most likely created the database user with a 127.0.0.1 host and are trying to connect from a different host.

`Access denied for user '_______'@'_______'`:
You either entered a wrong password or something is wrong with the database user you entered. Make sure that the database user exists and has the required permissions.

---

# Change Panel Domain

> Move the Pelican Panel to a new domain by updating the webserver config, APP_URL in .env and the remote URL in each node's Wings config.

Source: https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/change-panel-domain/

Moving the Panel to a new domain means changing it in three places: your webserver config, `APP_URL` in the Panel's `.env` file, and the remote URL in each node's Wings config.

## Webserver & Panel

First you need to modify the server name in your web server config.

### Nginx

```sh
sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-available/pelican.conf
# Search for "server_name"
```

> **Info: Using HTTPS?**
>
> If you're using HTTPS, remember to also change the SSL paths in the config file to match your new domain and [generate a new certificate](https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/ssl/).

### Apache

```sh
sudo nano /etc/apache2/sites-available/pelican.conf
# Search for "ServerName"
```

> **Info: Using HTTPS?**
>
> If you're using HTTPS, remember to also change the SSL paths in the config file to match your new domain and [generate a new certificate](https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/ssl/).

### Caddy

```sh
sudo nano /etc/caddy/Caddyfile
```

Next, modify the `APP_URL` in the `.env` file located at `/var/www/pelican` by typing `sudo nano /var/www/pelican/.env`.

Finally, restart your webserver to apply the changes.

### Nginx

```sh
sudo systemctl restart nginx
```

### Apache

```sh
sudo systemctl restart apache2
```

### Caddy

```sh
sudo systemctl restart caddy
```

## Nodes

The wings config file for each node must be updated to match the new Panel URL. (`remote` field)

You can do it manually in the `config.yml` file located at `/etc/pelican` or overwrite it completely by copying it from the Panel.

Make sure to restart wings (`sudo systemctl restart wings`) after updating the wings config file.

---

# Uninstalling

> Remove the Pelican Panel and Wings from a host, including panel files, webserver config, queue worker, database, Wings service and server data.

Source: https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/uninstalling/

This guide will show you how to uninstall the Pelican Panel and Wings. Note that the uninstallation of dependency services is not covered here.

> **Danger**
>
> **You will lose all data and this action is irreversible!**

## Panel

### Panel files

First, run the following command to delete all panel files.

```sh
sudo rm -rf /var/www/pelican
```

### Webserver config

Next, remove the Pelican webserver config.

#### NGINX

```sh
sudo rm /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/pelican.conf
sudo rm /etc/nginx/sites-available/pelican.conf

systemctl restart nginx
```

#### Apache

```sh
sudo rm /etc/apache2/sites-enabled/pelican.conf
sudo rm /etc/apache2/sites-available/pelican.conf

systemctl restart apache2
```

#### Caddy

```sh
sudo rm /etc/caddy/Caddyfile

systemctl restart caddy
```

### Queue worker service

Finally, remove the queue worker service.

```sh
systemctl disable --now pelican-queue
sudo rm /etc/systemd/system/pelican-queue.service
```

### (Optional) Panel database

If you used MySQL/ MariaDB and also want to remove the panel database, run the following commands:

```sh
mysql -u root -p

DROP DATABASE panel;
DROP USER 'pelican'@'127.0.0.1';
```

## Wings

### Wings service

To uninstall Wings you just have to remove the wings service, delete the wings binary and delete the wings config file.

```sh
systemctl disable --now wings
sudo rm /etc/systemd/system/wings.service

sudo rm /usr/local/bin/wings
sudo rm -rf /etc/pelican
```

### (Optional) Server data & backups

If you also want to remove all server files and backups run the following command:

```sh
sudo rm -rf /var/lib/pelican
```

---

# Migrating from Pterodactyl

> Upgrade a Pterodactyl install to Pelican in place, keeping users, servers, nodes and eggs, with the Panel and Wings migration scripts or Docker.

Source: https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/migrating-from-pterodactyl/

Pelican upgrades your Pterodactyl database in place: users, servers, nodes, eggs, databases, backups, schedules, subusers and API keys all carry over.
Your game servers keep running and keep their files.

> **Danger: Back up first**
>
> The migration changes your database and can't be undone. Back up your database, `/var/www/pterodactyl` and `/etc/pterodactyl` before you start.
> If anything goes wrong, ask on [Discord](https://pelican.dev/discord).

## Requirements

- Pterodactyl 1.11.4 or newer. [Update Pterodactyl](https://docs.pterodactyl.io/v1/panel/updating) first if needed.
- The [Panel dependencies](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/standalone/getting-started/#dependencies), including PHP 8.4 or newer with PHP-FPM.

## Migrate the Panel

### Script

Download the script and run the checks. They change nothing and tell you exactly what to fix, like a PHP version that's too old or a missing extension.

```sh
curl -fsSLo migrate-panel.sh https://pelican.dev/migrate-panel.sh
sudo bash migrate-panel.sh --check
```

Once every check passes, run the migration:

```sh
sudo bash migrate-panel.sh
```

It installs Pelican in `/var/www/pelican`, copies your `.env` and upgrades the database. It also sets up the queue worker and cron job. Your old install stays untouched in `/var/www/pterodactyl`.

Last, [point your webserver](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/standalone/webserver-config/) at `/var/www/pelican/public` and disable the Pterodactyl site.

### Docker

Take Pterodactyl offline first, so nothing writes to the database:

```sh
cd /var/www/pterodactyl
sudo php artisan down
sudo systemctl disable --now pteroq
```

Then remove the Pterodactyl `schedule:run` line from `sudo crontab -e`.

Create the `compose.yml` from the [Docker guide](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/install/#create-composeyml) and add these to its `environment`:

```yml
APP_INSTALLED: "true" # upgrade the database instead of opening the web installer
DB_CONNECTION: mysql # or mariadb on MariaDB. Without it Pelican falls back to SQLite
# Only if MySQL and Redis run on this machine:
DB_HOST: host.docker.internal
REDIS_HOST: host.docker.internal
```

If you use `host.docker.internal`, MySQL and Redis must listen on the Docker network (not only `127.0.0.1`), and your database user must be allowed to connect from `172.20.0.0/16`.

Copy your Pterodactyl `.env` into the container before its first start:

```sh
docker compose create
docker compose cp /var/www/pterodactyl/.env panel:/pelican-data/.env
```

The container serves the Panel on ports 80 and 443, so stop the webserver that served Pterodactyl first (for example `sudo systemctl disable --now nginx`).

Start it. The database is upgraded on startup, so wait for that to finish before seeding:

```sh
docker compose up -d
until docker compose logs panel | grep -q "Starting Supervisord"; do sleep 2; done
docker compose exec panel php artisan db:seed --force
```

If the wait never ends, the upgrade failed. Check `docker compose logs panel`.

## Migrate Wings

Run this on every node. It checks everything first, then swaps in Pelican Wings and keeps your existing config and server files.

```sh
curl -fsSLo migrate-wings.sh https://pelican.dev/migrate-wings.sh
sudo bash migrate-wings.sh
```

## What changes

- **Nests and locations become tags.** Eggs get a tag with their old nest name and nodes get one with their old location.
- **API keys keep working**, including old `ptla_`/`ptlc_` keys. The nests and locations API endpoints are gone, see the [API docs](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/advanced/api-docs/).
- **Root admins** get the Root Admin role.
- **Themes and panel modifications** don't carry over. Look for a [plugin](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/advanced/plugins/) instead.

<details>
<summary>Migrating by hand</summary>

Use this instead of the scripts if you want to run each step yourself.

**Stop Pterodactyl and back up the database.**

```sh
cd /var/www/pterodactyl
sudo php artisan down
sudo systemctl disable --now pteroq
sudo crontab -e   # remove the line running /var/www/pterodactyl/artisan schedule:run
grep '^DB_' .env
mysqldump -h <DB_HOST> -P <DB_PORT> -u <DB_USERNAME> -p --single-transaction --no-tablespaces <DB_DATABASE> > ~/pterodactyl-backup.sql
```

**Install Pelican.** Follow the [Standalone Install](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/standalone/getting-started/) up to (and including) **Install Composer**, but don't run the web installer. Then copy your `.env` and upgrade the database. Make sure `.env` has `DB_CONNECTION=mysql`, or `DB_CONNECTION=mariadb` on MariaDB: Pterodactyl didn't need it, but without it Pelican falls back to SQLite.

```sh
sudo cp /var/www/pterodactyl/.env /var/www/pelican/.env
cd /var/www/pelican
sudo php artisan optimize:clear
sudo php artisan migrate --seed --force
```

`HASHIDS_SALT`, `HASHIDS_LENGTH`, `APP_THEME` and `APP_ENVIRONMENT_ONLY` are no longer used and can be removed from `.env`.

**Finish the setup.** [Set permissions](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/standalone/panel-setup/#setting-permissions) and [configure your webserver](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/standalone/webserver-config/). Then set up the queue worker and cron job, and bring the Panel up:

```sh
sudo php artisan p:environment:queue-service
(sudo crontab -l -u www-data 2>/dev/null; echo "* * * * * php /var/www/pelican/artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1") | sudo crontab -u www-data -
sudo php artisan up
```

**Wings**, on every node:

```sh
sudo systemctl stop wings
sudo curl --fail -L -o /usr/local/bin/wings "https://github.com/pelican/wings/releases/latest/download/wings_linux_$([[ "$(uname -m)" == "x86_64" ]] && echo "amd64" || echo "arm64")"
sudo chmod u+x /usr/local/bin/wings
sudo mkdir -p /etc/pelican
sudo cp /etc/pterodactyl/config.yml /etc/pelican/config.yml
```

Update `/etc/systemd/system/wings.service` to match the one in [Installing Wings](https://pelican.dev/docs/wings/install/#daemonizing-using-systemd) (the working directory is now `/etc/pelican`), then run `sudo systemctl daemon-reload` and `sudo systemctl start wings`.

</details>

---

# Translating Pelican

> Help translate the Pelican Panel on Crowdin, including how approval works, how to handle placeholders and plurals and how to request a new language.

Source: https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/translating/

The Panel is translated by the community on [Crowdin](https://crowdin.com/project/pelican-dev). Anyone can help, no coding needed.
There is no minimum a language has to reach: whatever is translated ships, and missing strings fall back to English.

> **Info**
>
> This covers translating the Panel itself. The documentation site is only available in English.

## Getting started

1. Create a Crowdin account and join the [pelican-dev project](https://crowdin.com/project/pelican-dev).
2. Pick your language and start translating strings in the Crowdin editor.

Please do **not** open pull requests that change files in `lang/` by hand. Translations are synced from Crowdin automatically and manual changes get overwritten.
The English source strings live in `lang/en/**/*.php` in the [panel repository](https://github.com/pelican/panel). If you add new strings in a code contribution, add them to `lang/en` only.

## Approval

Only **approved** translations are shipped. Proofreaders review suggested translations for their language and approve them.

If your language has no proofreader, or you want to become one, ask in the Crowdin project discussions or on our [Discord](https://discord.gg/pelican-panel).

## Placeholders and plurals

Keep placeholders exactly as they are in the English string.

- **Placeholders** start with a `:` and get replaced with a value. Don't translate or remove them, but you can move them around in the sentence.

    ```php
    'greeting' => 'Hello :name!',
    ```

- **Plurals** are separated by `|`. In English the first part is the singular and the second the plural. Use as many forms as your language needs, in the order your language's plural rules expect. Explicit ranges like `{0} No files|[1,*] :count files` work too.

    ```php
    'model_label' => 'Backup Host|Backup Hosts',
    'create' => 'Created <b>:files</b>|Created <b>:count</b> new files',
    ```

- Keep HTML tags like `<b>` as they are, only translate the text between them.

## Requesting a new language

Ask for the language to be added in the Crowdin project. Once it has approved strings it shows up in the Panel with the next sync.

Most languages need no code changes. Only languages with a regional code need a mapping in [`crowdin.yml`](https://github.com/pelican/panel/blob/main/crowdin.yml) (`languages_mapping`), for example `zh-CN` → `zh_CN` and `pt-BR` → `pt_BR`.

## How translations reach the Panel

Two GitHub workflows in the panel repository keep Crowdin and the code in sync:

- **Upload Crowdin Sources** (`upload-sources.yml`) runs on every push to `main` that changes `lang/en/**` or `crowdin.yml`, and uploads the English strings to Crowdin.
- **Download Crowdin Translations** (`download-translations.yml`) runs every Sunday at 00:00 UTC (and can be started manually). It downloads all approved translations, formats them with Pint and opens a "New Crowdin Translations" pull request from the `i18n_crowdin_translations` branch.

After that pull request is merged, the translations are part of the next release.

## Languages in the Panel

Every language folder in `lang/` can be selected on the user's profile page, plus languages provided by plugins.
Languages other than English show a note that they may not be fully translated, with an "Update On Crowdin" link back to the project.
Any string that isn't translated yet is shown in English.

---

# Troubleshooting

> Diagnose common Pelican problems: panel 500 errors and logs, Wings connection issues, schedules not running, file uploads and plugin removal.

Source: https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/troubleshooting/

Start here when something in Pelican doesn't work. This page shows where to find the Panel's logs and how to fix common Panel errors, Wings connection problems, schedules that don't run, failing file uploads and plugins that won't uninstall.

## Panel errors

If you see a `500 | SERVER ERROR` or `An unexpected error was encountered while processing this request` you have to check your panel logs by running the following command.

```sh
tail -n 1000 /var/www/pelican/storage/logs/laravel-$(date +%F).log | grep "\[$(date +%Y)"
```

<details>
    <summary>Common errors</summary>

    * `ErrorException: file_put_contents(_____): failed to open stream: Permission denied`: Wrong file permissions/ ownership for the panel files, see [below](#wrong-file-permissions).
    * `502 Bad Gateway Error`: Make sure that php-fpm is running and that you are using the correct php version in your webserver config.
    * `CSRF token mismatch`: Enable SSL for your Panel with HTTPS protocol scheme in the `APP_URL`, or set `SESSION_SECURE_COOKIE` to `false` in your `.env` file.
    * `Connection refused [tcp://_______:6379]`: Redis isn't running or isn't reachable for some other reason. (start by checking the status of the redis service: `systemctl status redis-server`)
    * `SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name '_______'`: The used SSL certificate for your panel isn't valid for your panel domain, see [this guide](https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/ssl/) for creating a new SSL certificate.
    * `General error: 8 attempt to write a readonly database`: Your `database.sqlite` has wrong file permissions and is read-only. Make sure the file is writable and owned by the correct user.
    * `Class '_____' not found`: This usually means you are missing php extensions. Make sure [all needed extensions](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/standalone/getting-started/#dependencies) are installed and that you are using the correct php version.
    * `Connection timed out after 5001 milliseconds for _______:8080`: Your panel can't reach wings, see the wings connection issues steps below.
</details>

### Wrong file permissions

If the command above doesn't return anything, you most likely have incorrect file permissions . So you first need to fix that.
You can set the correct permissions by running `sudo chmod -R 755 /var/www/pelican/storage/* /var/www/pelican/bootstrap/cache/`. Also make sure that your panel files are owned by the correct user.

#### NGINX/Apache

```sh
sudo chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/pelican
```

#### Rocky Linux NGINX

```sh
sudo chown -R nginx:nginx /var/www/pelican
```

#### Rocky Linux Apache

```sh
sudo chown -R apache:apache /var/www/pelican
```

## Wings connection issues

### Check the wings service

First you should make sure that the wings service is running. To do that run `systemctl status wings`.
It should say that the service is active and running. If its in a failed state run `sudo wings diagnostics` to check the wings logs for errors.

<details>
    <summary>Common errors</summary>

    * `open /etc/letsencrypt/live/_____________/fullchain.pem: no such file or directory`: The SSL certificate for wings is missing, see [this guide](https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/ssl/) for creating a SSL certificate.
    * `Pool overlaps with other one on this address space`: You already have a docker network using the default subnet. (`172.18.0.0/16`) Change the subnet in your wings config file and use `systemctl stop wings && docker network rm pelican_nw && systemctl start wings` to apply the change.
    * `Error response from Panel: AccessDeniedHttpException: You are not authorized to access this resource. (HTTP/403)`: Your wings token is wrong, you need [update the token in your config.yml file](https://pelican.dev/docs/wings/install/#configure)
    * `Error response from Panel: _MissingResponseCode: No error response returned from API endpoint`: Your panel is not responding correctly. This usually happens when Cloudflare is blocking the connection. In that case make sure your wings ip is added to the Cloudflare firewall. If you aren't using Cloudflare it might be some other CDN/ DDoS protection service or your provider.
    * `remote: could not unmarshal response: invalid character '<' looking for beginning of value`: This is basically the same error as above: Cloudflare is blocking the connection.
</details>

### Check the wings port

If you confirmed that wings is running without errors you should make sure that the wings port (`8080` by default) isn't blocked by any firewall. The best way to check this is to use online port checkers like [dnschecker.org](https://dnschecker.org/port-scanner.php)
It should say "open" if you check for your node FQDN (e.g. `node.example.com` or `123.123.123.123`) and your wings port (e.g. `8080`). If it says "timed-out" you have some firewall blocking the port. This could be an internal firewall (like iptables) or an external firewall (e.g. from your provider).

### Check for NAT loop back

If your panel and wings are on the same machine or same network, and you are using domains you should check for NAT loop back issues.
Edit the `/etc/hosts` file on your panel/ wings machine and add an entry for your ip and domain.

Example:

```txt title="/etc/hosts"
123.123.123.123 panel.example.com node.example.com
```

### Check the wings connection

If you confirmed the above points you have to do some advanced troubleshooting.

Check if your panel and your browser can connect to wings.

#### Panel \<-> Wings connection

Run `curl <protocol><node fqdn>:<node port>` (e.g. `curl https://node.example.com:8080` or `curl http://123.123.123.123:8080`) on your panel machine and see what it outputs.

#### Browser \<-> Wings connection

Open `<protocol><node fqdn>:<node port>` (e.g. `https://node.example.com:8080` or `http://123.123.123.123:8080`) in your browser and see what it outputs.

In both cases it should output this when wings is reachable:
```
{"error" : "The required authorization heads were not present in the request."}
```

> **Info**
>
> Not sure what a specific error means?
> Visit our [Discord](https://discord.gg/pelican-panel) and we will be happy to help you!

### Check node settings

If the connection checks above were both successfull you might have misconfigured the Node settings in the Panel.
Make sure that your Node FQDN/ IP, Port and Scheme (HTTP/ HTTPS) is correct.

When using a reverse proxy you might have different external and internal ports for Wings. (e.g. `80` internally and `443` externally)
In that case make sure the Node settings in the Panel uses the external port while the Wings config file uses the internal port!

## Schedules not running

If your Schedules are stuck on `Processing` or don't execute the tasks check the following:

* Is your Schedule set to run `ONLY WHEN SERVER IS ONLINE` and the server is currently offline?
* Is your queue worker service running? (`systemctl status pelican-queue`)
* Is your queue worker service using the correct PHP version? (`php -v`)
* Is your cronjob setup correctly? `crontab -l -u www-data` (where `www-data` is your webserver user) should show the following entry:
`* * * * * php /var/www/pelican/artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1`

If your queue worker service is not running you can also check the panel logs for errors.

```sh
tail -n 100 /var/www/pelican/storage/logs/laravel-$(date +%F).log | grep "\[$(date +%Y)"
```

To recreate the queue worker service you can run `php /var/www/pelican/artisan p:environment:queue-service --overwrite`.

## File Upload issues

If a file upload form returns an error like `mountedActionsData.0.files.24d4b82d-a3ae-47fd-981f-8b2f0f6a21d4` it is most likely a proxy issue.

Make sure your `Trusted Proxies` are set to the correct ips, both in the panel settings and your proxy settings!
Also make sure your webserver and/ or proxy have a high enough upload limit. (e.g. `client_max_body_size`, `upload_max_filesize` and `post_max_size`)

In some cases the issue can also be caused by incorrect file permissions. See [above](#wrong-file-permissions) on how to fix your file permissions.

## Plugin uninstalling issues
If you can't uninstall a plugin via the admin panel, you may have to do it via ssh.
Navigate to the root application directory: `/var/www/pelican/` and run this command:
```sh
php artisan p:plugin:uninstall
```
It will ask for which plugin you want to remove and if you want to delete its data.
Uninstalling may take a few seconds

After all this, try visiting the plugins page on the admin dashboard. If you see any 500 error, setup permissions back running this command on the root directory (`/var/www/pelican/`):

### NGINX/Apache/Caddy

```sh
sudo chown -R www-data:www-data /var/www/pelican
```

### Rocky Linux NGINX

```sh
sudo chown -R nginx:nginx /var/www/pelican
```

### Rocky Linux Apache

```sh
sudo chown -R apache:apache /var/www/pelican
```

---

# About Quotas

> Read the warnings and requirements before enabling filesystem disk quotas for Pelican server data, which are still a work in progress.

Source: https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/disk-quotas/about/

Disk quotas let the filesystem limit how much space each server's files can use. Support for them in Pelican is still a work in progress, so read the notices on this page before you enable them.

> **Tip**
>
> As called out in the Wings install docs, it is always recommended to keep the server files on a separate partition.

## There are a lot of notices here for a reason!

> **Danger**
>
> Support for disk quotas is still being worked on!

> **Warning**
>
> These are advanced configurations meant for hosts but "should" work for individuals as well.

> **Warning**
>
> Depending on the filesystem Quotas can be difficult to enable for the `/` mount, which requires booting a live disk to change.

> **Info**
>
> You can either make a new mount with quotas enabled or enable quotas on an existing partition.

## Filesystem-specific docs
[EXT4/XFS](https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/disk-quotas/ext4-xfs/)

---

# EXT4 and XFS

> Enable project quotas on a new or existing EXT4 partition for Pelican server data, then create projects and set and check quota limits.

Source: https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/disk-quotas/ext4-xfs/

This page covers disk quota management for EXT4/XFS.

Both EXT4 and XFS use the built-in quota management services in linux.

> **Warning**
>
> Please read [About Quotas](https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/disk-quotas/about/) before continuing

## Configure Filesystem
How to format and mount a device for use with quotas

<details>
<summary>I understand the risks and Pelican is not Liable for anything that breaks</summary>

> **Warning**
>
> Enabling quotas for `/` is difficult, as it requires booting a live disk to change.
>
> We do not recommended this!

These examples use the following:
`/dev/sdb` as the device formatted as EXT4 enabling only project quotas.
`/var/lib/pelican/volumes/` as the mount point and data directory

### New EXT4 Filesystem

## Format Device
`mkfs.ext4` will format the disk with the ext4 filesystem
* The `O` flag is the enable Feature Options
  - enable quotas while formatting
* The `E` flag is for Extended Options
  - set the quota type as project
```bash
mkfs.ext4 -O quota -E quotatype=prjquota /dev/sdb
```

> **Warning**
>
> You need to update fstab so the disk mounts automatically on boot with quotas enabled.

## Add to fstab
### get device UUID
The disk UUID is the best option for mounting the correct device via fstab.
```bash
lsblk /dev/sdb -no UUID
# example output
6c3b1734-3db4-4368-9bee-58651731b206
```

### add new mount to fstab
```shell title="/etc/fstab"
# <file system> <mount point>   <type>  <options>       <dump>  <pass>
# / was on /dev/sda1 during installation
UUID=8529a07b-28bc-4296-848a-a185aaf11e94 /               ext4    errors=remount-ro 0       1
UUID=6c3b1734-3db4-4368-9bee-58651731b206 /var/lib/pelican/volumes/ ext4 defaults,prjquota 0 1
```
For more information on fstab check the [Arch Linux fstab docs](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Fstab)

> **Warning**
>
> Depending on the OS you may need to refresh services to be able to mount the partition after updating `fstab`.
>
> It is often easier to reboot and have the disk mount on boot.

### Existing EXT4 Filesystem

## Update existing partition
Get the disk device path and uuid for your partition

by default `findmnt` lists all mounts on the system and lists their source, fstype, and options
* The `n` flag disables headers
* The `o` flag only returns specified values
  - `SOURCE` is device path
  - `UUID` is the device id
```bash
findmnt /var/lib/pelican/volumes -no SOURCE,UUID
## example response
/dev/sdb 6c3b1734-3db4-4368-9bee-58651731b206
```

## Unmount disk
Use `umount` to unmount Pelican's volume mount.
```bash
umount /var/lib/pelican/volumes/
```

## Enable quotas

> **Warning**
>
> This can only be ran on an unmounted disk

`tune2fs` is used to adjust tunable file system parameters for EXT filesystems
* The `Q` flag is to manage quotas
  - `prjquota` is to enable project quotas
* The device path is needed
```bash
tune2fs -Q prjquota /dev/sdb
```

## update fstab entry
add `prjquota` to the line for the mount
from
```shell title="/etc/fstab"
UUID=6c3b1734-3db4-4368-9bee-58651731b206 /var/lib/pelican/volumes/ ext4 defaults 0 1
```
to
```shell title="/etc/fstab"
UUID=6c3b1734-3db4-4368-9bee-58651731b206 /var/lib/pelican/volumes/ ext4 defaults,prjquota 0 1
```
For more information on fstab check the [Arch Linux fstab docs](https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Fstab)

> **Warning**
>
> Depending on the OS you may need to refresh services to be able to mount the partition after updating `fstab`.
>
> It is often easier to reboot and have the disk mount on boot.

</details>

## Advanced EXT4 Quota Management

> The following section is for manual management of quotas.

## Manually Manage Quotas
Limits for the servers are managed on a "project" level so they can be assigned per-directory.

### Add A New Project
To add a new project 2 files must be edited.

First is the `projid` file which is formatted where each line is in the `project_name:project_id` format as seen below
* Pelican will use the server UUID as the project name
* Make sure the ID is not already being used.
```shell title="/etc/projid"
235844d3-9258-4846-bb04-bcff209ccf9a:1
b91d5528-d53f-4586-8d5c-682027f74a36:2
```

Second is the `projects` file which is formatted where each line is in the `project_id:path_to_directory` format as seen below
```shell title="/etc/projects"
1:/var/lib/pelican/volumes/235844d3-9258-4846-bb04-bcff209ccf9a
2:/var/lib/pelican/volumes/b91d5528-d53f-4586-8d5c-682027f74a36
```

### Set directory attributes
The project attribute must be set on the directory to track quota usage.

The `chattr` command changes attribute for files and directories.
* The `+` and `-` operators add or remove attributes
  - The `P` makes it so files and directories created in the directory will inherit the project id of the directory.
    - The project id and directory must match
* The `p` flag is for the project id
```bash
chattr +P -p ${project_id} ${path_to_directory}
```

Example:
```bash
chattr +P -p 1 /var/lib/pelican/volumes/235844d3-9258-4846-bb04-bcff209ccf9a
```

### set quota limits
The built in quota management uses blocks by default.
* You can specify limits in bytes as well.

The `setquota` command sets the quota for any object that supports quotas.
* The `P` flag sets the quota for a project
  - This can use the project `id` or `name`
  - The should be the server UUID as shown in the examples below
* The soft limit would send a warning to a user
  - This is not used by Pelican and will be set to 0
* The hard limit is set to the disk resource limit set in Pelican
* Neither the block or inode/file grace sections will be used by Pelican.
* The path for either the device or the mount point
  - `/dev/sdb/` or `/var/lib/pelican/volumes/`
```bash
setquota -P ${server_uuid} ${soft_limit} ${hard_limit} ${block_grace} ${inode_grace} ${path}
```

Example:
setting a hard limit, in Gigabytes
```bash
setquota -P 235844d3-9258-4846-bb04-bcff209ccf9a 0 10G 0 0 /var/lib/pelican/volumes/
```

### get quota stats
The `repquota` command will generate a report on the quotas for the specified device or mount path
* The `P` flag will break down the report by project.
  - In this case it should be the server UUID that is the project name
* The `--human-readable` flag sets the limits to be displayed in a human readable format. By default that is Megabytes
  - `=g,g` changes the output to be in Gigabytes (can be `k`, `g`, `m`, or `t`)

Example:
```bash
repquota -P --human-readable=g,g /var/lib/pelican/volumes/ # could also be /dev/sdb
```

Example Output
```shell
                        Block limits                File limits
Project         used    soft    hard  grace    used  soft  hard  grace
----------------------------------------------------------------------
235844d3-9258-4846-bb04-bcff209ccf9 --      3G      0G      5G             1g    0g    0g
cdb26bbb-963d-44b1-8353-360243032b1 --      2G      0G      2G             1g    0g    0g
```

</details>
</details>

>

# Versioning & Releases

> How Pelican versions the Panel and Wings with semantic versioning, what counts as a breaking change, and how deprecations, releases and support work.

Source: https://pelican.dev/docs/versioning/

Pelican follows [semantic versioning](https://semver.org/) (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`).

## Panel and Wings

The Panel and Wings are versioned **independently**. A Panel release does not mean there is a Wings release with the same number, and the other way around.
Compatibility is guaranteed within a major version: any Panel `1.x` works with any Wings `1.x` at or above the Panel's minimum Wings version.
See [Updating the Panel](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/update/) and [Updating Wings](https://pelican.dev/docs/wings/update/) for the current requirements.

| Panel   | Minimum Wings |
|---------|---------------|
| `1.0.x` | `1.0.0`       |

The minimum Wings version is only raised in a **minor** Panel release and is announced in the release notes.

The Panel checks the Wings version of every node and shows two kinds of warnings:

- **Outdated**: the node runs an older Wings than the latest release. It still works, but you should [update Wings](https://pelican.dev/docs/wings/update/).
- **Incompatible**: the node runs a Wings older than the Panel's minimum. The node icon turns yellow, the node page shows the required version and the health check fails. Update Wings as soon as possible.

The Panel never blocks a node because of its Wings version. An incompatible node keeps working, but features that need a newer Wings may fail.

## What semver covers

A breaking change to any of these only happens in a new **major** version:

- The REST API: the [application and client API](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/advanced/api-docs/), both request inputs and response shapes.
- The egg format (egg export/import) and the requirements for [yolks](https://pelican.dev/docs/eggs/creating-a-custom-yolk/).
- Configuration: the Panel `.env` keys and the Wings `config.yml` format.
- The plugin API, as described in the [plugin compatibility policy](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/advanced/plugins/#compatibility-policy).

These are **not** covered and can change in any release:

- The database schema. It is internal, use the API instead of querying tables directly.
- Internal PHP classes, services and views not listed in the plugin compatibility policy.
- The UI.

## Deprecations

Features, API fields and config keys are deprecated in a **minor** release and removed only in the next **major** release.
Deprecations are announced in the release notes and marked as deprecated in the [API docs](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/advanced/api-docs/).

Minimum requirements (PHP, database versions) are only raised in minor releases and are announced in the release notes.

## Releases

Releases are tagged from the `main` branch.

- **Patch** releases (`1.0.1`) contain bug and security fixes.
- **Minor** releases (`1.1.0`) add features and can deprecate things.
- **Major** releases (`2.0.0`) can remove deprecated things and make other breaking changes.

The changelog lives in the GitHub releases:

- Panel: [github.com/pelican/panel/releases](https://github.com/pelican/panel/releases)
- Wings: [github.com/pelican/wings/releases](https://github.com/pelican/wings/releases)

## Support

Only the **latest release** is supported. Bug and security fixes ship as a new patch release, they are not backported to older versions.
Please [update](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/update/) before reporting a bug.

## Upgrading from a beta

Update like any other release, following [Updating the Panel](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/update/) and [Updating Wings](https://pelican.dev/docs/wings/update/).
Upgrading from `1.0.0-beta38` or earlier to `1.0.0` includes these breaking changes:

> **Warning: PHP 8.4 required**
>
> PHP 8.3 is no longer supported. [Upgrade PHP](https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/php-upgrade/) **before** updating the Panel.

### Application API

API responses are unchanged, but some deprecated request inputs were removed:

| Endpoint                                   | Removed input                                           | Use instead         |
|--------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| `PATCH /api/application/servers/{id}/build` | `memory`, `swap`, `io`, `cpu`, `threads`, `disk`        | `limits.*`          |
| `POST /api/application/servers`            | `deploy.locations`                                      | `deploy.tags`       |
| `GET /api/application/nodes/deployable`    | `location_ids`                                          | `tags`              |

The removed inputs are **silently ignored** on the build and deployable endpoints, so check any scripts or billing integrations that still send them.

### Discord webhooks

Discord support moved out of the core webhook system into plugins.
Existing Discord webhooks keep firing with their saved payload, but lose the Discord-specific formatting (such as embed timestamps) and can't be edited.
Install a plugin that provides the Discord webhook type to edit them or create new ones.

### Plugins

- Fractal was removed. `App\Transformers\Api\*` and `$this->fractal` are gone; API responses are built with the classes in `app/Data/Api` and `$this->response`.
- `App\Enums\WebhookType` and the `DiscordPreview` component were removed. Webhook types are now plain strings.
- Activity logs are append-only. Updating or deleting an `ActivityLog` throws an exception.
- Major dependency updates: `phpseclib/phpseclib` 4, `predis/predis` 3, `spatie/laravel-permission` 8 and `spatie/laravel-query-builder` 7. Check your plugin code and `composer_packages`.
- `^` in `panel_version` now works like composer's caret and stops before the next major version. See [Panel version](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/advanced/plugins/#panel-version).

### Passkeys

If passkey sign-in fails after updating and the Panel runs behind a reverse proxy, set `TRUSTED_PROXIES` (see [Reverse Proxy Setup](https://pelican.dev/docs/panel/standalone/optional-config/#reverse-proxy-setup)) so the Panel sees the correct host.

# Pelican vs Pterodactyl and other game panels

> Compare Pelican with Pterodactyl and other game server panels such as PufferPanel, Crafty Controller, TCAdmin, AMP and Calagopus.

Source: https://pelican.dev/docs/comparison/

Pelican is a free, open-source game server control panel built on modern Laravel and Filament.
It started as a fork of Pterodactyl and has since grown well beyond it.

## Why Pelican?

* **Make it yours** with plugins and themes from the [Hub](https://hub.pelican.dev)
* **Up and running in minutes** with Docker or the web installer
* **Modern logins** with passkeys, OAuth (11 providers) and two-factor authentication
* **Give staff exactly the access they need** with admin roles and permissions
* **Speak your users' language** with 32 languages, translated by the community
* **Keep backups safe** on S3 or local storage, configured per node

> **Tip: Already on Pterodactyl?**
>
> Migrate in place and keep your servers, users and data. Follow the [migration guide](https://pelican.dev/docs/guides/migrating-from-pterodactyl/).

> **Info: Try it yourself**
>
> See everything below in action on our [Demo](https://demo.pelican.dev)!

## What's new compared to Pterodactyl

### General

* First party Plugin system
* Roles & Permissions for Admins
* Webhooks
* Health page (cache, database, queue, scheduler, disk and version checks)
* Your own logo and favicon
* Replace Nests & Locations with Tags
* Improved Settings page
* Customization for Users (e.g. Server list layout, Console font)
* Config option for Binary Prefix (MiB/GiB)
* ![In Progress](https://img.shields.io/badge/In_Progress-orange) Rework allocations
* ![Planned](https://img.shields.io/badge/Planned-blue) More database types for Database Hosts

### Frontend

* Rewrite of Client Area in Filament
* Rewrite of Admin Area in Filament
* Available in 32 languages, translated by the community
* Light and dark mode
* User avatars
* Timezone configurable per User
* Switch from Webpack to Vite

### API

* Integrated API docs
* Application API for Database Hosts
* Application API for Server Transfers
* Application API for Mounts
* Uniform user transformers
* Rename `oom_disabled` to `oom_killer`

### Auth

* Passkeys
* OAuth with 11 providers, plus automatic account creation and linking
* Email two-factor alongside TOTP
* Replace Google reCAPTCHA with Cloudflare Turnstile

### Setup

* Easier Installation process (Web Installer)
* Dockerized Installation
* Egg selection during install
* PostgreSQL as Panel database
* SQLite as Panel database
* "Proper" support for MariaDB as Panel database (dedicated driver)
* Easier Database Host setup via Step-by-Step Wizard

### Server

* Server icons
* Per-server webhooks
* Backup-completed notifications
* Global search for files
* View install logs from within the Panel
* Activity log for server crashes
* Easier Schedule Cron setup
* "Delete files" schedule task
* Servers without Allocations
* IPv6 Support for Allocations
* Custom docker labels for server containers
* Delete backups when server is deleted
* ![Planned](https://img.shields.io/badge/Planned-blue) Server sorting

### Node

* Multiple backup hosts (local or S3), assigned per node
* Node diagnostics and one-click log upload
* Node resource statistics
* Node Ownership (assign nodes to roles)
* Disk quotas for servers
* CPU Limit for Nodes
* Automatically fetch Node IPs for easier Allocation setup
* Better proxy support
* Alias for SFTP address
* Automatic cleanup of dangling docker images
* Fixed `-1` overallocation

### Eggs

* Browse and import eggs from the panel
* Multiple startup commands per egg, selectable by users
* Easier Egg updating (usage of `update_url`)
* Import multiple eggs at once
* Sortable egg variables
* Change Egg format to YAML

### Hub

* Marketplace for Plugins & Themes
* Marketplace for Eggs
* Open Finances
* Support Tickets
